spec: Validate a password: it must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least 3 of the following 4 character classes: lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, and special (non-alphanumeric) characters. Return False if fewer than 3 classes are present or the password is too short.

Given a list of (x, y) integer coordinate tuples and a target (tx, ty) tuple, sort the points ascending by Manhattan distance from the target, defined as abs(x-tx) + abs(y-ty). Ties are broken by x ascending, and further ties by y ascending.
Determine whether an integer n is a perfect square (equal to k*k for some non-negative integer k). Negative numbers are never perfect squares.

Validate a UPC-A barcode: a string of exactly 12 digit characters. Compute the check digit as follows: sum the digits in odd positions (1st, 3rd, ..., 11th, 1-indexed) and multiply by 3, add the sum of digits in even positions (2nd, 4th, ..., 12th); the total must be divisible by 10 for the code to be valid. Return False if the string is not exactly 12 digits.
Given two dates date1 and date2 as (year, month, day), return True if they represent the exact same calendar date, otherwise False.

Find the values in the list items that occur more than once. Return a sorted list of those distinct values (each listed once, regardless of how many times it repeats). An empty list, or a list with no repeats, returns an empty list.
Given a string of whitespace-separated words, count how many of the words are palindromes when compared case-insensitively (the word reads the same forwards and backwards ignoring letter case).

Given a list of distinct integers, compute the minimum number of swaps needed, where each swap can exchange any two elements, to rearrange the list into descending order. Return that minimum count as an integer. An empty list or an already-descending list requires 0 swaps.

Given two lists of integers that are each already sorted in descending order, merge them into a single descending list containing all elements from both (duplicates are kept). When elements are equal, an element from the first list comes before an equal element from the second list. Either list may be empty.

Zero-pad the non-negative integer n to the given width, then split the resulting digit string into consecutive chunks of the given group size (the last chunk may be shorter) and join the chunks with hyphens.
Given a string s, return the sum of all its digit characters interpreted as individual digits 0-9, ignoring any non-digit characters. A string with no digits returns 0.
For a positive integer n, return the smallest power of two that is greater than or equal to n.
Replace every occurrence of the reserved Windows filename characters < > : " / \ | ? * with an underscore, then strip any trailing spaces or period characters from the end of the resulting name.

Format a count with a noun, using the singular form of the word when the count is exactly 1 and otherwise pluralizing it with simple English rules (s/x/z/ch/sh get 'es', consonant+y becomes 'ies', otherwise add 's'), producing a string like '3 cats'.
Write a function that returns the length of the longest run of consecutive equal elements in a list. An empty list has a longest run length of 0.
Format a number as US currency: two decimal places, comma thousands separators, and a leading dollar sign, with the minus sign (if the amount is negative) placed before the dollar sign.

Given the current time and an event's start time, both as 'HH:MM' strings on a 24-hour clock, return the number of minutes until the event starts. If the event's time has already passed today (i.e. is earlier than or equal to the current time, but not exactly equal), assume it occurs at that time tomorrow instead. If the times are exactly equal, return 0.
Given a list of value strings and a column width, right-align each value within that width and join them with the separator ' | '.

Write a function that counts the number of maximal 'plateaus' in a list of numbers, where a plateau is a run of two or more consecutive equal elements. Runs of length one do not count. Return the number of such plateaus as an integer; return 0 for an empty list.

Given a list of (department, name, salary) records, return the list of names ordered so that department comes first alphabetically. Within a department, order by salary from highest to lowest, and if salary also ties, order alphabetically by name. The input list may be empty.
Given a list of (name, score) tuples, build a dict mapping each distinct name to the highest score recorded for it in the list. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Format an integer with an explicit sign: prefix positive numbers with '+', leave negative numbers as-is (with their existing minus sign), and format zero as the plain string '0' with no sign.

Given a list of 2-element tuples, group the second elements by the first, preserving the order in which they appeared (including duplicates). Return a dict mapping each distinct first element to a list of its corresponding second elements. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of numbers and a target number, sort the list by absolute distance from the target, closest first. When two numbers are equally distant from the target, the smaller number comes first. An empty list returns an empty list.

Validate a grouped hexadecimal string: it must consist of one or more groups of exactly 2 uppercase hexadecimal digits (0-9, A-F) each, with groups separated by a single underscore, and no leading, trailing, or double underscore. Return False otherwise.

Write a function that returns the running (cumulative) maximum of a list of numbers as a new list of the same length, where each output element is the largest input value seen up to and including that position. An empty input produces an empty output.

Given two dates date1 and date2 as (year, month, day), with date2 on or after date1, return the number of whole calendar months elapsed from date1 to date2 (the day of month is ignored except that if date2's day is earlier in the month than date1's day, the current partial month does not count).

Validate a mention string used to tag another user. It must start with '@' followed by a username: 3 to 16 characters, the first an alphabetic letter, the rest letters, digits, or underscores. Return False otherwise.

Write a function that inserts a given value into a list at a specified index, shifting subsequent elements to the right, and returns the resulting list. Assume 0 <= index <= length of the list (index equal to the length appends at the end).
submission:
def insert_at_index(lst, idx, value):
    result = list(lst)
    result.insert(idx, value)
    return result

spec: Extract all numeric digit characters from a string, in their original order, and return them concatenated as a string. If the string contains no digits, return an empty string.

Given a list of numbers and a positive integer k that is at most the length of the list, return the maximum possible sum of any k consecutive elements in the list. Assume the list has at least k elements.
Given a year and two month numbers month1 and month2 with month1 <= month2, return the total number of days across all months from month1 to month2 inclusive of that year, accounting for leap years.

Count the number of lines in a string, where lines are separated by newline characters. An empty string has zero lines; otherwise the count is one more than the number of newline characters in the string.
Convert a non-negative integer n into its binary representation as a string of '0' and '1' characters, with no leading zeros (except that 0 itself maps to "0").
Count how many perfect squares lie in the inclusive integer range [a, b], where 0 <= a <= b.

Join a list of strings into a natural-language list with 'and' before the last item. If any item itself contains a comma, use semicolons as the separators instead of commas (to avoid ambiguity), otherwise use commas as normal; the oxford-style separator before 'and' follows the same rule for three or more items.
visible_tests: assert oxford_join_semicolon(['Tokyo, Japan', 'Paris, France']) == 'Tokyo, Japan and Paris, France'

spec: Return True if the given string is a valid combined date and time in strict "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" format (a valid ISO date, a single space, then a valid HH:MM:SS time with hours 0-23), and False otherwise.
Count the number of characters in a string that are neither alphanumeric (letters or digits) nor whitespace, such as punctuation and other symbols.

Given a date string "YYYY-MM-DD" and an integer n (which may be negative), return the ISO date string "YYYY-MM-DD" of the date n days later, correctly handling month and year boundaries and leap years.
Count how many prime numbers are less than or equal to a non-negative integer n.
